data.title: Daily Voice: Large-cap valuations at historic lows signal further market upside, says Narnolia CIO
data.description:
Shailendra Kumar is the Chief Investment Officer at Narnolia Financial Services
  • Large-cap valuations remain in lowest quartile of their long-term historical range
  • Expect broader market to take longer to regain leadership over large caps
  • RBI could consider a 25-basis-point rate hike in December meeting
Did our AI summary help?

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Large-cap valuations remain in the lowest quartile of their long-term historical range, providing a favourable valuation backdrop for the market rally to sustain and potentially extend further, said Shailendra Kumar, Chief Investment Officer at Narnolia Financial Services, in an interview with Moneycontrol.

He expects the broader market to take longer to regain leadership over large caps, as mid- and small-cap valuations remain relatively expensive.

Meanwhile, with October CPI inflation rising above 6 percent, the RBI could consider a 25-basis-point rate hike, he said. However, if global commodity and energy inflation moderate, he expects the rate hike to be followed by an extended pause.

Is the frontline index-led market rally sustainable, given the weakness in the broader markets?

Frontline indices have rallied over 15 percent from their early-October lows, supported by a strong Q2FY27 corporate earnings season. More importantly, large-cap valuations remain in the lowest quartile of their long-term historical range, providing a favourable valuation backdrop for the rally to sustain and potentially extend further.

Will corporate earnings and the Union Budget be the key drivers in sustaining the ongoing market rally?

A: Indian corporate earnings have remained strong since early 2026, supported by the consumption recovery following last year’s GST cuts and a renewed momentum in both public and private capex. Nifty 50 earnings growth was limited to mid-single digits during FY25 and FY26, but since Q4FY26, growth has consistently moved closer to 20 percent YoY, signaling a meaningful improvement in the earnings cycle.

Despite this recovery, persistent FII outflows—driven by stronger earnings growth in markets benefiting from the AI investment cycle and concerns over India’s fiscal and macroeconomic position amid the US-Iran conflict—had kept Indian equities subdued. However, India’s resilience in navigating significant geopolitical disruptions is gradually changing investor sentiment.

While the Union Budget may influence near-term market direction, we believe the sustainability of the rally will ultimately be determined by corporate earnings. As long as earnings momentum remains strong, the underlying foundation of the ongoing market rally remains intact.

Do you expect broader markets to take longer to outperform largecaps?

Yes, we expect the broader market to take longer to regain leadership over large caps. The earnings growth differential between small-cap and large-cap companies has narrowed significantly during the Q2FY27 earnings season.

However, mid- and small-cap valuations remain in relatively expensive territory, while large caps continue to trade at attractive, below-average valuations. This valuation gap is likely to favour large caps in the near term.

Which sectors are you structurally bullish on at the moment?

We remain structurally bullish on auto components, precision engineering, healthcare services, insurance, capital markets and banks.

Beyond these sectoral preferences, we maintain strong conviction in leading companies across industries. We believe several of these Indian industry leaders have the potential to evolve into global champions, emerging as dominant players in their respective industries worldwide—what we term “World Toppers.”

Is this the right time to bet on the FMCG sector, given its recent performance and growth prospects?

The Nifty FMCG Index traded at a trailing 12-month P/E of around 30x in October, its lowest valuation level in nearly 15 years. The emergence of D2C brands has intensified competition, challenging the long-established pricing power and distribution-led moat of large listed FMCG companies. However, the funding environment for D2C businesses has moderated in recent times, easing competitive intensity.

Most emerging brands have also struggled to build sizeable franchises, with relatively few scaling to revenues of Rs 1,000 crore or more. Meanwhile, large listed FMCG companies are increasingly willing to acquire emerging brands, strengthening their competitive positioning and widening their portfolio of growth opportunities.

Despite these improving structural dynamics and the sharp around 20 percent rally in FMCG stocks recently, we remain somewhat cautious in the near term, given the uncertain inflation outlook. We believe the sectors bottoming-out process may take longer to play out, although the downside from current levels appears relatively limited.

Do you think AI-led disruption could continue to weigh on valuations in the Indian equity market?

AI-led disruption has been increasingly visible in the IT services sector over the past two years. At a broader level, we believe AI is a positive structural development for businesses, with the potential to enhance productivity and support earnings growth across industries.

However, in the Indian context, the more important question is its eventual impact on white-collar employment and the resulting second-order implications for consumption. While the situation remains encouraging so far, these developments warrant close monitoring as AI adoption accelerates.

Is credit growth nearing its peak for banks? What is your preferred segment within the financial sector?

We believe the banking sector has entered a structural phase of above-trend credit growth, with NIMs also poised to improve from current levels. This strengthens our preference for banks within the financial sector.

We remain equally constructive on select insurance and capital market businesses, which offer attractive long-term structural growth opportunities.

Do you expect the RBI to keep the repo rate unchanged in its December policy meeting, while the US Federal Reserve delivers another rate hike?

With October CPI rising above 6 percent, the RBI could consider a 25 bps rate hike. However, if global commodity and energy inflation moderate, we expect this to be followed by an extended pause.

Meanwhile, the hawkish tone of the US Federal Reserve’s October policy minutes strengthens our expectation of a further 25 bps rate hike by the Fed.

International Gemological Institute, which certifies diamonds, coloured stones and jewellery, achieved the minimum public shareholding (MPS) requirement on November 27 after promoter Blackstone, through its affiliate, offloaded a 1.55 percent stake in the company through open-market transactions.

According to block deal data on Friday, BCP Asia II Topco, an affiliate of Blackstone, sold 67.16 lakh equity shares of International Gemological Institute for Rs 280.05 crore. The transaction represented 1.55 percent of the company's paid-up equity capital.

Seven institutional investors, including Stallion Asset and Old Bridge Mutual Fund, acquired the entire stake sold by Blackstone at Rs 417 per share.

Stallion Asset purchased 11.98 lakh equity shares of International Gemological Institute for Rs 49.97 crore, while Old Bridge Mutual Fund acquired 24 lakh shares for Rs 100.08 crore. Citigroup Global Markets Singapore purchased 7.19 lakh shares for Rs 30 crore.

Additionally, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore, Susquehanna Pacific, Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust and WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund each acquired 5.99 lakh shares for Rs 25 crore.

Following the 1.55 percent stake sale, the total shareholding of the promoter and promoter group in International Gemological Institute declined from 76.55 percent to 75 percent of the paid-up equity share capital, while public shareholding increased to 25 percent, the company said in its filing.

Accordingly, the company has achieved the minimum public shareholding requirement.

Shares of International Gemological Institute rose 1.52 percent to close at Rs 429.65 on Friday, after declining 4.8 percent from the day's high.

Aegis Investment Fund buys 0.5% stake in Jagran Prakashan

Meanwhile, Aegis Investment Fund purchased 11 lakh shares of Jagran Prakashan, representing 0.5 percent of its paid-up equity capital, for Rs 7.61 crore.

The shares were purchased at Rs 69.19 apiece.

Jagran Prakashan stock staged a stellar performance on Friday, surging 9.5 percent to Rs 68.26 amid high trading volumes. The stock extended its gains for the third consecutive session.

Tiger Strategies Fund sells shares worth Rs 12 crore in Shalimar Paints

Tiger Strategies Fund-I offloaded 11 lakh shares of Shalimar Paints for Rs 11.88 crore. The shares were sold at Rs 108.01 apiece.

However, Shalimar Paints shares rose 0.43 percent to Rs 108.57, extending their upward trend for the fourth consecutive session. The rally was accompanied by high trading volumes, particularly following a gap-up opening on November 23.

data.title: US stocks rebound as traders pile into battered tech shares
data.description:
-
  • US stocks rallied on Friday, led by tech and chip shares.
  • S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 headed for their best weeks since May.
  • Investors remain cautious amid AI sustainability and rate fears.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

US stocks rallied Friday, capping a week of whiplash as dip buyers scooped up some beaten down technology shares despite lingering worries about the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence boom.

The S&P 500 Index was up 1.2% as of 10:53 a.m. in New York, while the Nasdaq 100 Index advanced 1.7% after US markets reopened from Thursday’s holiday. Trading will end early at 1 p.m. in New York on Friday.

Stocks have swung sharply this week, with Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s chief executive officer and Anthropic PBC’s brief fall below its IPO price adding to volatility across the AI trade. Anthropic jumped 8.4% Friday. A key gauge of market turbulence — the Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX — was around 26 after briefly spiking to nearly 35 on Wednesday, when markets tumbled early in the session before clawing back the losses.

Nvidia Corp. fell as much as 2.6% and was the biggest point decliner in both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100. But a gauge of chip stocks rebounded along with other AI beneficiaries, including data-storage firm SanDisk Corp., which soared 13%, and Micron Technology Inc., which gained 5.7%. Optical-products maker ​Lumentum Holdings Inc. and server maker Dell Technologies Inc. both gained at least 6%.

The advance left the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 heading for their best weeks since May. The most speculative corners of the market were higher Friday, with Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s basket of the most-shorted stocks rising 1.5% — with its 7.2% weekly gain on track for its best since August — while a basket of unprofitable tech companies jumping 2.6%.

“Despite any rebounds, this is the most nervous half day of trading for investors that we’ve seen in years, given that there’s not a lot of conviction around Nvidia still,” said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president, head of retail expansion and alternative investment products at Cboe Global Markets.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave Inc. was flat, reversing an earlier sharp rise, while Nebius Group NV rose 2.5% to ease off earlier highs after jumping nearly 6%. AI hyperscalers Meta Platforms Inc. rallied more than 3% while Amazon.com Inc. jumped 2.8%. Apple Inc. rose nearly 1%. Oracle Corp. advanced 1%. A basket of Magnificent Seven stocks rose 1.6%, putting its weekly gain of 7.3% on track for its best since April.

US Chipmakers Rebound

Even with this week’s rebound, the S&P 500 is eyeing its worst November since the height of the 2008 financial crisis as the market is dragged down by concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom, elevated inflation and expectations that the Federal Reserve will resume raising interest rates next month.

Swap traders are almost fully pricing in a quarter-point ​rate hike in December after data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in ​the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October.

“There’s still fierce debate over whether the AI trade is over or not,” said Michael Antonelli, market strategist at Baird. “Institutions will have to make decisions in the next few weeks over how to move forward and that will set the tone heading into 2027.”

President Donald Trump has also sowed uncertainty with tariff hikes planned on imports from China, Japan, the European Union and other trading partners. Key events to watch next week include Huang’s congressional testimony following his reinstatement at Nvidia and the November US jobs report.

Traders remained optimistic Friday, though, as strong profit outlooks during the crucial holiday season would present a much-needed tailwind. Estimates from the National Retail Federation imply a 4.2% growth in holiday retail sales in 2026 from a year ago, compared with 3.1% in 2025. On Black Friday alone, Americans are expected to spend almost $13 billion in online transactions, data from Adobe Analytics shows.

So far, earnings results from retail companies have been mixed. Earlier this week, Dollar Tree Inc.’s third-quarter adjusted earnings per share and comparable sales topped Wall Street expectations, while Best Buy Co. Inc. raised its guidance for the year on resilient demand for computing. Target Corp.’s sales beat estimates, while TJX Companies Inc. narrowed its earnings outlook.

More retailers will report earnings next week, including Macy’s Inc. and Dollar General Corp.

On Friday, defensive stocks that tend to have comparatively low valuations and offer robust dividends were slipping after outperforming earlier in the week, with Coca-Cola Co., Procter & Gamble Co. and J.M. Smucker Co. all lower.

Investors had flocked to such consumer staples companies in the past few months, putting them on track for the best quarter since 2000. The advance has made valuations look stretched: the S&P 500 Consumer Staples Index is sitting at 24 times projected earnings, the most since the 1990s.

Sectors in Focus

Elsewhere, Altria Group Inc. fell as much as 2.6% after news that the company is considering an offer for British cigarette maker Imperial Brands, potentially in partnership with Japan Tobacco.

Meanwhile, Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc. slid 6.9% after the company said the FDA extended the target action date by up to three months for a license application for the use of povetacicept to treat a type of chronic kidney disease.

data.description:
Swaraj Green Power and Fuel IPO News
  • Swaraj Green Power and Fuel plans to raise Rs 1,100 crore via IPO
  • IPO Mix: Fresh issue of Rs 800 crore, OFS of Rs 300 crore
  • Company to use fresh issue mainly for debt reduction

Swaraj Green Power and Fuel, an ethanol production and sugar manufacturing company, has filed an updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), seeking to raise up to Rs 1,100 crore through its maiden public offering.

The Maharashtra-based company, headquartered in Satara, plans to raise Rs 800 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, while promoter Ranjeetsingh Hindurao Naik Nimbalkar has proposed to sell shares worth Rs 300 crore through an offer-for-sale (OFS).

The company may also consider raising up to Rs 160 crore through a pre-IPO private placement, which would form part of the fresh issue. Accordingly, if the pre-IPO placement is undertaken, the size of the fresh issue will be reduced by the amount raised through the placement.

Swaraj Green Power had initially approached the capital markets by filing its draft offer document through the confidential pre-filing route in March this year. Subsequently, the SEBI cleared draft papers in June 2026.

The company operates an integrated manufacturing facility in Maharashtra with a zero liquid discharge system. The facility has an installed sugarcane crushing capacity of 7,500 tonnes of cane per day (TCD), a cogeneration unit with a capacity of 636 MW and a distillery unit with a capacity of 500 kilolitres per day (KLPD).

Swaraj Green Power proposes to utilise Rs 620.8 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards repayment of debt against its outstanding borrowings of Rs 747.4 crore as of September 2026. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

On the financial front, Swaraj Green Power reported a standalone profit of Rs 13.1 crore on revenue of Rs 352.5 crore for the three months ended June 2026. For the financial year ended March 2026, the company reported a profit of Rs 25.3 crore on revenue of Rs 1,021.6 crore.

data.title: SEBI allows FPIs to trade in physically settled commodity derivatives, puts in place risk safeguards
data.description:
• SEBI allows FPIs in physical non-agri derivatives.
  • FPIs must exit positions before delivery period.
  • New framework to take effect from June 1, 2027.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Market regulator SEBI has allowed foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to participate in physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, a move aimed at deepening institutional participation and improving market liquidity.

The relaxation comes with a risk-management framework to ensure that foreign investors exit their positions before the delivery period begins.

Under the revised framework, FPIs can trade in non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts, except options in goods, and indices comprising such derivatives. So far, their participation was restricted to cash-settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives.

FPIs can participate in physically settled contracts only up to the commencement of the tender or staggered delivery period. They must square off or roll over their open positions before the delivery period begins.

The primary responsibility for exiting positions will remain with FPIs. If they fail to do so by the close of market hours on the day preceding the tender period (T-1), their residual positions will automatically devolve upon a designated trading broker or trading-cum-clearing broker.

Related Stories

  • Ananya Birla-led Svatantra Microfin gets SEBI nod for Rs 3,000-crore IPO
  • SEBI clarifies 65-year age limit for MII managing directors remains unchanged
  • SEBI may revisit Rs 2 lakh retail investor limit in IPOs if warranted; ICDR working group to examine...

FPIs will have to enter into a tripartite agreement with the clearing broker and trading broker, or a bipartite agreement with a trading-cum-clearing broker. They can trade through multiple trading brokers but must have one designated trading broker or trading-cum-clearing broker under the framework.

Also read: SEBI may revisit Rs 2 lakh retail investor limit in IPOs if warranted; ICDR working group to examine issue

Risk management safeguards

SEBI has introduced safeguards to prevent delivery-related risks and ensure that designated brokers are prepared to absorb devolved positions.

Three trading days before the tender or staggered delivery period, FPIs cannot take fresh positions that increase their existing exposure in the expiring futures contract. Positions arising from the devolvement of options on futures upon expiry are exempt from this restriction.

Clearing brokers must also ensure that FPI positions are either squared off or transferred to designated brokers by the close of T-1. They must inform the designated broker by the end of T-2 about positions that could devolve, allowing sufficient time to arrange margins.

The transfer will take place after market closure on T-1, at the exchange-declared closing or daily settlement price, and will be treated as a normal market trade. Once transferred, the FPI will cease to have any rights, obligations or exposure relating to the position, including the tender and delivery process.

The designated trading broker or trading-cum-clearing broker will act as a risk-management intermediary and manage the devolved positions. SEBI has clarified that accepting such positions will not be treated as a business activity involving assumption of commodity exposure or proprietary trading by the broker.

The regulator has also allowed onboarding agreements to incorporate a pre-agreed Risk Absorption Charge, payable by the FPI if its positions devolve because it fails to exit voluntarily. The charge will compensate the designated broker for the risk, margin and position-limit burden. Its amount and calculation methodology must be disclosed and agreed upon at onboarding. It will be over and above any service fee and will not replace penalties imposed by exchanges or clearing corporations.

Further, exchanges may allow designated brokers up to two trading days to reduce positions within prescribed limits if devolved FPI positions push their proprietary accounts beyond permissible limits. Such positions will not attract position-limit violation penalties during this period.

Clearing corporations may also refrain from levying penalties on the first day for short or non-collection of margins arising from increased initial margin requirements due to devolved positions.

Exchanges and clearing corporations will standardise onboarding agreements, frame guidelines for the post-market closure window and ensure designated brokers have adequate visibility of positions and margin obligations.

The circular will come into effect from June 1, 2027.

Also read: SEBI summons APL Apollo officials over Tata Steel deal, examines possible RPT rule violations

Ananya Birla-led Svatantra Microfin, Sterlite Electric, Beauty Garage and Noble Hygiene are among eight companies that have received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to proceed with their initial public offering (IPO) plans. The capital markets regulator also cleared the draft offer documents of Gaurik Fashions, Emerald Jewel Industry India, MP Steel (India) and Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers.

Sterlite Electric filed its draft offer document with SEBI in October 2025 to raise funds through an IPO, followed by Gaurik Fashions in May 2026. Meanwhile, Svatantra Microfin, Noble Hygiene, MP Steel (India) and Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers filed their draft IPO papers in August 2026.

SEBI issued its observations on Sterlite Electric's draft offer document on November 20, followed by those of Gaurik Fashions and Beauty Garage on November 26. The regulator issued observations on the draft offer documents of Emerald Jewel Industry India, Svatantra Microfin, Noble Hygiene, MP Steel (India) and Kataria Dhulchand Pannalal Jewellers on November 27, according to the processing status of draft offer documents published for the week ended November 27.

data.title: Technical View: Cooling momentum signals further consolidation in Nifty 50; 25,300 key support for next week, Bank Nifty must hold 62,500
data.description:
NIfty outlook for November 30, 2026
  • Weakness below 25,500 and 25,300 would be required for bears to take control
  • Otherwise, the broader market structure remains favourable for the bulls
  • On the upside, 25,800 and 26,000 remain crucial resistance levels
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

The Nifty 50 witnessed a correction throughout the session on November 27 after gaining for a couple of sessions, falling over 1 percent. However, the index continued to trade within Monday's wide range of 25,300–26,000 for the third consecutive session.

The weakness appears to be part of a consolidation phase at higher levels and a cooling-off in momentum following the recent strong rally of around 17 percent. Consistent weakness and a decisive breakdown below the 25,500 and 25,300 support levels would be required for bears to take control. Otherwise, the broader market structure remains favourable for the bulls, with the index sustaining above all key moving averages. The short- and medium-term moving averages also continue to remain above the long-term moving averages.

On the upside, 25,800 and 26,000 remain crucial resistance levels. A decisive move above these hurdles could pave the way for a rally towards the record high zone of 26,350–26,400, according to market experts.

Momentum indicators point towards further consolidation and a weakening of bullish momentum. The RSI declined from overbought territory to 65.47 and remained below its signal line. However, it continued to hold above the 60 mark, keeping the broader momentum in the bullish zone.

The MACD remained above its signal line, indicating that the underlying trend strength is still intact. However, it continued to slope downwards towards the signal line, with the green histogram bar contracting for the 13th consecutive session. Together, these indicators suggest that bullish momentum is gradually losing strength, increasing the likelihood of further consolidation.

Related Stories

  • Taking Stock: Market snaps 4-week rally; Nifty below 25,650, Sensex sheds 989 pts
  • Black Friday: Sensex settles 1,000 pts lower, Nifty ends near 25,600; 5 key factors behind market cr...
  • Sensex, Nifty Near 10-Month High | US futures tick higher | Brent crude tops $96 | Opening Bell

According to Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities, the considerable gap between the spot price and short-term moving averages leaves room for further consolidation and intermittent profit booking.

The Nifty 50 opened lower and, after initial volatility, remained under pressure for most of the session. The index declined 277 points, or 1.07 percent, to close at 25,607. On the daily charts, it formed a long bearish candle with minor upper and lower shadows, highlighting selling pressure at higher levels.

However, "the overall bullish chart pattern remains intact and present weakness could be an opportunity to create longs at the lows. Bullish chart pattern like higher tops and bottoms is unfolding on the intraday timeframe chart and current weakness is likely to form a new higher bottom of the pattern," said Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities.

On the weekly chart, the Nifty formed a reasonable bearish candle near the highs after a stellar four-week rally, declining 0.75 percent. This indicates consolidation at higher levels. Despite trading close to its record highs, there are no significant signs of a reversal pattern emerging near the resistance zone, Nagaraj said.

According to him, the short-term correction is likely to end by next week. The immediate support to watch is around 25,300, while the crucial overhead resistance is placed at 26,000.

The weekly options data also point to 26,000 as a crucial resistance level, with the highest Call open interest concentrated at this strike. The 25,800 strike, which has the next-highest Call open interest, is likely to act as an immediate hurdle.

On the downside, the 25,500 strike, which has the next-highest Put open interest, is likely to provide immediate support. The 25,000 strike, with the highest Put open interest, remains a crucial support level for the index.

Meanwhile, India VIX, the market's fear gauge, declined another 1.72 percent to 16.55. However, it remained elevated and would need to move towards the 14 zone for volatility to ease meaningfully and market stability to improve. Until then, volatility is expected to remain high, warranting caution among market participants.

Bank Nifty

The banking index remained under pressure for the second consecutive session amid profit booking, ending 0.78 percent lower. It formed a small-bodied bearish candle with an upper wick, highlighting selling interest at higher levels.

Bank Nifty witnessed a decline of 890 points from the day's high, reflecting strong supply at elevated levels. However, it continued to trade within Monday's wide range of 62,500–65,200 for the third consecutive session.

The broader positional structure remains bullish, with the recent weakness appearing to be a cooling-off phase following the strong rally.

The RSI continued to decline from overbought territory but remained in the bullish zone at 66.01. The ADX remained elevated, supporting the underlying trend strength. The MACD also remained comfortably above its signal line despite sloping slightly downwards, while the green histogram bar contracted for the fourth consecutive session.

On the weekly chart, Bank Nifty declined 2.47 percent and formed a long bearish candle, indicating profit booking following a four-week rally that had taken the index to a record high.

"The significant gap between spot levels and short-term EMAs suggests scope for further consolidation and a moderation in momentum. The 62,400–62,500 zone is expected to act as immediate support. A sustained breakdown below this range could intensify profit booking towards 62,000," said Sudeep Shah, Head - Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities.

On the upside, the 63,500–63,600 zone remains the immediate resistance area, he added.

data.description:
• SEBI clarifies MD age limit remains 65 years.
  • Proposed reducing single MII tenure to eight years.
  • Cumulative tenure across MIIs capped at 12 years.
Did our AI summary help?

Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Friday clarified that its November 20 consultation paper on strengthening the governance of market infrastructure institutions (MIIs) does not propose any change to the maximum age limit of 65 years for their managing directors (MDs).

The clarification follows media reports suggesting that SEBI was considering a change in the age limit for MII managing directors.

SEBI said consultation papers set out proposals only for provisions where changes are intended. Provisions for which no change is proposed are not included in the paper.

The maximum age limit of 65 years for MII MDs remains unchanged. The proposals in the consultation paper relate only to their term and tenure at a single MII and across different MIIs.

Also read: SEBI may revisit Rs 2 lakh retail investor limit in IPOs if warranted; ICDR working group to examine issue

Related Stories

  • SEBI may revisit Rs 2 lakh retail investor limit in IPOs if warranted; ICDR working group to examine...
  • Sensex, Nifty down 0.5% this week; Brent above $98, Rupee at 93/$ | Closing Bell
  • SEBI summons APL Apollo officials over Tata Steel deal, examines possible RPT rule violations

In the consultation paper, SEBI has proposed reducing the maximum tenure of an MD at a single MII from 10 years to eight years, while capping cumulative tenure across MIIs at 12 years, with a maximum of three terms. For MDs already in office when the proposed rules take effect, the regulator has suggested a cumulative tenure cap of 15 years across institutions, while allowing them to complete their ongoing terms.

The proposals aim to address concerns over concentration of authority, prolonged dependence on individual executives and key-man risk at market infrastructure institutions, which perform important regulatory functions.

SEBI also clarified that a Public Interest Director (PID), MD or Executive Director (ED) holding office on the date the proposed amendments come into effect would continue in office until the end of their ongoing term.

The consultation paper has been issued for public comments, and SEBI said decisions on the proposals would be taken only after the consultation process. Stakeholders can submit comments and suggestions through SEBI's website until December 11, 2026.
